sentences.text: One minute of latitude equals one nautical mile, about six thousand seventy-six feet, roughly fifteen percent longer than a statute mile.
A knot is a speed of one nautical mile per hour, so never say knots per hour.
Minutes of longitude are a nautical mile long only at the equator and get shorter toward the poles, which is why you never measure distance on the longitude scale.
Modern charts and GPS units divide minutes into tenths, while older charts show seconds.
